text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — hosted-api us-east experiencing sustained queue growth. backlog=12,300 reqs, p95=3.2s, p99=12.7s. GPU pool healthy=3/10, autoscaler reported errors. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-growth
ops_oncall (emma): ack — I'm taking lead. Paging @sre_lead.
sre_lead (ben): on call, joining. What are the autoscaler errors?
ops_oncall (emma): logs show repeated `provisioner: rate_limit_exceeded` and `CreateInstance: QuotaExceeded`. Also controller restarted once; leader-election timeout around 1005123400. Posting small log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T02:10:12Z provisioner: create_instance failed status=429 QuotaExceeded project VMCreatePerMin
2026-03-17T02:11:08Z controller: leader election timeout, restarting
```
infra (carla): confirmed cloud project is hitting VM create QPS quota. I've opened a quota escalation with cloud team (ticket 8942). ETA to bump ~15-30m, may be expedited.
devex (matt): can we temporarily route traffic to smaller quantized model to reduce GPU concurrency? I can flip routing rules.
sre_lead (ben): yes, do it now. Also apply per-customer burst caps for top traffic groups to slow new inflow. Commands:
```
# switch fallback for generate route in us-east
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --model small-quant-v2 --route /v1/generate --region us-east
# limit top customer burst
redwoodctl rate-limit update --selector customer:high-traffic --qps 0.5
```
ops_oncall (emma): executed fallback flip and rate-limit. dashboard shows GPU concurrency down ~40% within 60s. current backlog 8,950.
support (alan): drafting customer note in #customers-incidents: "We saw elevated latencies due to infrastructure quota limits. We've temporarily routed traffic to a smaller model and applied burst limits for some customers; you should see improvement in 5-15 minutes. We're monitoring and will follow up." Approve to send?
sre_lead (ben): approve, send.
support (alan): sent to affected tenants.
ops_oncall (emma): queue now 6,200 and draining. p95 down to 1.1s. Still seeing some timeouts at p99 from long-waiting requests.
infra (carla): starting emergency attach of dedicated thinpool (dedicated-reserve-dus) as hot spare to us-east; authorizing manual pool attach now. ETA ~6m.
incident-bot: Reminder — runbook step 4: consider temporary capacity from Dedicated / reserved pools and enable request prioritization.
infra (carla): pool attach succeeded at 1005123680. +4 GPU nodes added to hosted pool.
ops_oncall (emma): confirmed +4 nodes live; backlog halved to ~2,900 and p95=0.8s. Good signal improving.
devex (matt): client-side SDK telemetry shows fewer retries. I'll mark the routing change in change-log and schedule rollback when capacity normalizes.
sre_lead (ben): next actions: 1) keep fallback routing for 10m after backlog drains, 2) follow up with cloud quota ticket owner for permanent quota increase, 3) add autoscaler backoff and better error classification in next sprint, 4) create prewarm run for planned campaigns. Assigning owners in postmortem.
support (alan): customers notified; no escalations so far.
ops_oncall (emma): summarizing: root cause = cloud VM create quota hit -> autoscaler unable to add nodes -> backlog growth. Mitigations = routing to smaller model, burst caps, manual attach of reserved pool. Outcome = queue drained, p95/p99 improving. Will file incident and postmortem.
sre_lead (ben): will own postmortem. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for now. Link to incident page: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1005123456
